title: Nasal vowels
description: Polish's two nasal vowels, ą and ę — a feature English has no equivalent to.

items.description: Nasalized mid back rounded vowel, spelled ą. Before a stop consonant it is usually pronounced as a plain vowel plus "m" or "n" (dąb sounds close to "domb").
Nasalized mid front unrounded vowel, spelled ę. At the end of a word it is frequently denasalized to a plain "e" in everyday speech.
